import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    corr_threshold = 0.6
    keep_ids = []
    used = set()
    
    # Build correlation matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if fid in used:
            continue
        keep_ids.append(fid)
        # Mark correlated features as used
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= corr_threshold:
                used.add(feats.ids[j])
    
    # Select top features by t-test
    t_stats = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(keep_ids):
        col = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, col]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, col]
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)
        t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
    
    # Sort by t-statistic and limit to MAX_DRIVERS-1 to ensure we can have at most 4 drivers
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1]
    driver_indices = sorted_indices[:MAX_DRIVERS-1] if len(sorted_indices) >= MAX_DRIVERS-1 else sorted_indices
    drivers = tuple(keep_ids[i] for i in driver_indices if t_stats[i] > 3.0)
    
    # Ensure we don't exceed 4 drivers
    if len(drivers) > 4:
        drivers = drivers[:4]
    
    # Select features for regression using mutual information
    mi_scores = mutual_info_classif(feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in keep_ids]], feats.y)
    selected_indices = np.argsort(mi_scores)[::-1][:len(keep_ids)//2]
    columns = tuple(keep_ids[i] for i in selected_indices)
    
    # Check for interactions among top features
    products = []
    top_features = list(columns[:5])
    for i, a in enumerate(top_features):
        for b in top_features[i+1:]:
            # Add interaction if both features have strong effect
            if a in drivers and b in drivers:
                products.append((a, b))
    
    # Create loadings (weighted sum of top features)
    loadings = dict(zip(columns, mi_scores[selected_indices]))
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
